motd: Type 'help' for the commands, 'man <command>' for one of them.
Your files are in /home/{user}. The rest of the disk is the system's.
help: files     ls cd pwd cat head wc touch mkdir rmdir rm cp mv echo find du
system    uname uptime date ps kill free df dmesg whoami id hostname history
other     sha1sum sleep clear color man help shutdown reboot
Keys: Tab completes, Up/Down history, Ctrl+C stops, Ctrl+L clears, wheel scrolls back.

man.ls:
ls [-l] [-a] [path...]
  List a directory. -l: long form, with owner, size and date. -a: also the hidden (dot) files.
man.cd:
cd [dir]
  Change the working directory. No argument: your home. '..' is the directory above.
man.cat:
cat file...
  Print files. /proc/cpuinfo and /proc/meminfo describe the hardware and its memory now.
man.head:
head [-n N] file
  Print the first N lines of a file (10 by default).
man.wc:
wc file...
  Count lines, words and bytes.
man.touch:
touch file...
  Create empty files, or update their time.
man.rm:
rm [-r] path...
  Remove files; -r also directories with everything in them. There is no undo.
man.cp:
cp src dst
  Copy a file. It is read off the disk and written back, and takes as long as the drive needs.
man.mv:
mv src dst
  Move or rename a file or directory.
man.echo:
echo text [> file | >> file]
  Print text, or write it to a file (> replaces it, >> adds to its end).
man.find:
find [dir] [-name pattern]
  Walk a directory tree and print every path in it (or those whose name matches; * matches anything).
man.du:
du [-s] [path]
  Disk usage of a tree, in KB.
man.uname:
uname [-a]
  The system's name (-a: with the kernel, the host and the machine).
man.uptime:
uptime
  Time since boot, and the load.
man.ps:
ps
  The processes in memory: id, user, resident memory (KB) and name.
man.kill:
kill pid
  Stop a process. Only your own; the system's belong to root.
man.free:
free [-m]
  Memory: total, used by the kernel and the processes, free. A program that does not fit in what is free does not start.
man.df:
df [-h]
  Disk space: size, used, available.
man.dmesg:
dmesg
  The kernel's messages since boot.
man.hostname:
hostname
  This machine's name on the network.
man.history:
history
  The commands typed in this session.
man.lshw:
lshw
  The hardware: processor, memory, disk, network adapters.
man.ifconfig:
ifconfig [iface]
  The network interfaces and their addresses.
man.iwconfig:
iwconfig
  The wireless interface: the network it is joined to, the signal.
man.sha1sum:
sha1sum file...
  A file's SHA-1 checksum. It reads the whole file: slow on a big one.
man.man:
man command
  The manual page of a command.
man.shutdown:
shutdown
  Halt the system and power off. The next time the lid opens, it boots again.
